body:
Tuning controls currently submit complete observed policies, so a stale edit can overwrite a keyboard learned or edited since that observation. Apply only the fields the user changed, with keyboard derivation performed by the configuration owner against its adopted fifth. Fixes #1406.

This also removes three sources of unnecessary work without adding caches or new runtime owners:

- Share the existing canonical ordering rules between the tracker, recorder and take parser. Parsing validates payloads in file order, then checks stable time order using three counters per source instead of reconstructing voices, release tails and roll history.
- Expand adaptive candidates once per distinct context node and reject candidates that cannot earn a snap before harmonic scoring. Preserve keyboard-pool precedence, exact output rounding and tie-breaking.
- Adopt a complete analyzer configuration once. Only window-size changes replan FFT resources; taper changes retain the plan, new channels start at final settings, and source restarts clear audio without constructing an intermediate estimator.

Snapshots and saved musical settings keep their complete policy representation. The runtime edit mask fits an unused word in the existing fixed-size mailbox. The intended behavior correction is that untouched fields survive concurrent/queued edits, and an explicit Derive action uses the current fifth even when its displayed snapshot looks already derived.

Validation:

- Independent domain reviews and a fresh combined review found no remaining defects; fixture reach was checked and strengthened for malformed duplicates and retained stereo channels.
- Local workspace tests with `nice-plug/assert_process_allocs`: 1,523 passed, 17 ignored before the clean rebase onto current main. Focused core, take, recorder and analysis suites also passed.
- Regressions cover stale Learn versus UI edits, queued disjoint packed fields and keyboard primes, atomic derivation, canonical duplicate/cut/error precedence, FFT-plan reuse with exact fresh-analyzer output, layout replacement and hop-phase retention.
- Optimized scratch scorer comparison: 3,000 exact decision matches; triad assignment about 4.51 → 2.26 µs, octave-doubled triad 7.11 → 2.25 µs. These are decision-level measurements, not whole-plugin latency.
- Scratch analyzer allocation counts per adoption: stereo taper-only 36 → 2; window plus tapers 72 → 36; alternating channel/layout/final-setting changes 76 → 31 on average. Rate-only and unchanged settings allocate zero in both versions. Timing was noisy, so no precise analyzer latency claim is made.

Final-head `Full CI` (workspace and isolated), `Metal shader assets`, and `Security audit` all passed, with GitHub reporting a clean merge state. Local `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the final analyzer suite also passed.

Both `harmonigraph-plugin` and `harmonigraph-offline` release builds succeeded. The plugin binary was read back with `load-plugin.sh --tag` and reports `codex/architecture-simplifications @90dbf18c`.

The four implementation commits are independent and worth preserving with a merge commit.
